artboards.title: One — the thumbnail is the whole widget

annotations.text:
THE DIVISION OF LABOR

Agent: every word. Which one, why, how long, what's different about it.

Widget: thumbnails. Nothing else — no title, no date, no channel, no snippet, no frame.

The prose on each artboard is real assistant phrasing, not filler. Retype it on the canvas to hear other wordings.

THIS COLLAPSES THE VIEW SYSTEM

Once the widget holds no text, "card" vs "spotlight" vs "carousel" stop being different components — they're one strip of thumbnails at different sizes:

1 → full width · 2–3 → split to fit · 4+ → fixed 172px, scrolls · fullscreen → same tile, wrapped

So the four view modes could become one responsive component. Worth deciding before I write the code — it deletes a lot of it.

THE ONE THING I KEPT

Duration. It rides on the image rather than around it, so it costs no layout, and the agent can't recite six durations in a sentence.

If you want it gone, the widget becomes literally just pictures — say the word.
Titles aren't deleted, just not drawn — each thumbnail carries its title in aria-label, so screen readers announce the video instead of "link, image". Visually absent, semantically present.
